sources.title: Contribution Déterminée au niveau National 3.0 du Maroc (2026-2035)
sources.organization: Kingdom of Morocco, Ministry of Energy Transition and Sustainable Development
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC 3.0 covers 2026-2035 and reports climate and disaster impacts through 2024, alongside longer-term climate projections.
sources.methodology: NDC compiles national risk and loss evidence and regional adaptation proposals.

sources.title: Plan National Stratégique d’Adaptation (PNSA-2030)
sources.organization: Morocco Ministry of Energy Transition and Sustainable Development, Department of Sustainable Development
sources.temporal_coverage: National plan for 2022-2030; combines observed climate trends, sector risk analysis and proposed adaptation measures.
sources.methodology: Plan assesses national and sector vulnerability and prioritizes adaptation actions.
sources.limitations: French text was translated for paraphrase; listed measures are proposals.

sources.title: Water Scarcity in Morocco: Analysis of Key Water Challenges
sources.temporal_coverage: National model uses a 2016 baseline and medium- to long-run water-supply and crop-yield scenarios.
sources.methodology: GTAP-BIO-W comparative-static model simulates national water and crop-yield shocks.
sources.limitations: Results are modeled, not observed, and provide no named local estimates.

sources.title: Morocco 2000003887: PADERMO Supervision Report February 2026
sources.temporal_coverage: Report dated 5 February 2026 on a supervision mission held 16-29 November 2025; implementation indicators generally reflect 31 October 2025.
sources.methodology: Joint 11-day supervision mission visited project sites and reviewed implementation, targeting and climate risks.
sources.limitations: French-language mission report; status reflects late 2025, not current delivery.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.62 (printed p.60), section 6, recent basin water deficits and climate impacts.
claims.paraphrase: 2022-23 deficits reached 81% in unnamed basins and cereal output fell 67%; the NDC records 50.4°C heat in Agadir and over 6,000 hectares burned in Oriental in 2023.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.65 (printed p.63), section 7.2, flood deaths, displacement and service disruption.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC reports over 100 flood deaths at Ourika (1995), 47 at Guelmim (2014), and nearly 22,000 internal displacements during 2008-2024.
claims.limitations: Displacements are not assigned to named events or cities.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The NDC frames the displacement total as climate-related.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.65-66 (printed pp.63-64), section 7.2, 2022 drought and agricultural losses.
claims.paraphrase: The 2022 drought caused up to 500,000 tonnes of fruit losses in Gharb, Haouz and Saïss; rural women faced disproportionate livelihood pressure.
claims.limitations: Labor and land shares are national.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It links drought-related farm precarity to rural exodus and women's migration.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.37-38 (printed pp.35-36), territorial adaptation plans and regional actions.
claims.paraphrase: Regional plans in Oriental, Drâa-Tafilalet, Souss-Massa, Béni Mellal-Khénifra and Marrakech-Safi target oasis and rural adaptation.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.106 (printed p.98), Annex 4, adaptation projects and human mobility.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC proposes wastewater reuse, groundwater management and water transfers to reduce water-stress migration.
affected_groups: people at risk of climate-related migration
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The NDC links these projects to lower migration.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.7, national climate circumstances and rainfall distribution.
claims.paraphrase: The plan reports 1960-2018 rainfall decline, warming and increased aridity; southern and southeast Atlas provinces are arid, while Souss, El Haouz and Oriental include semi-arid zones.
claims.limitations: Climate pattern descriptions are broad regional classifications.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.10, fisheries vulnerability and exposure assessment.
claims.paraphrase: By 2050, catch potential could fall 5% under RCP8.5; artisanal fishers, small aquaculture producers and women-majority fish processors are identified as especially exposed.
claims.limitations: The plan gives no locality-specific catch estimate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The plan attributes higher exposure to limited adaptive capacity and dependence on fishery resources for livelihoods and well-being.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.61-63 and 69-74, oasis and community-based adaptation actions.
claims.paraphrase: The plan proposes oasis livelihood diversification and climate early warning, and community-led vulnerability mapping and water options tailored to each mountain massif.
claims.limitations: These are plan measures, not verified implementation results.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.32-33 (printed pp.25-26), Table 6.3 and discussion of labor and migration.
claims.paraphrase: In modeled case SC4, a 25% water-supply reduction plus climate-related yield changes reduces national unskilled-labor demand by 7%; permanent losses may expand urban migration.
claims.scenario: SC4: 25% water-supply reduction combined with crop-yield shocks; report describes medium- to long-run effects.
claims.limitations: Model scenario, not a forecast of realized job losses or migration volumes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report says permanent water or yield losses may shrink farm jobs and expand migration to urban areas.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.25-26 (printed pp.18-19), National Irrigation Water Saving Program discussion.
claims.paraphrase: The 2020 report says the government program supports sprinkler and drip irrigation, targeting 555,000 hectares and a reduction in flood-irrigated land from 81% to 43%.
claims.limitations: Targets are reported in a 2020 paper and are not implementation results.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.6-7 (printed pp.3-4), sections C-D, mission conclusions on provincial project execution.
claims.paraphrase: The 2025 mission found cumulative delays, 9% effective physical execution and under 1% disbursement; it attributed slow progress partly to limited provincial agriculture-department capacity and delayed technical assistance.
claims.limitations: Status is from the November 2025 mission, not a 2026 progress update.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.17 (printed p.15), outreach indicators and planned target groups.
claims.paraphrase: The report records 5,651 activity participants, 45% women and 52% youth, against design targets of 30% and 40%; another section gives a different reach total.
geographies: 19 communes in Oujda-Angad, Berkane, Driouch and Guercif
claims.limitations: The report's reach totals differ across sections; figures reflect the 2025 mission.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.21 (printed p.19), sections on climate adaptation investments and Amejjaou rural road damage.
claims.paraphrase: Strong recent floods damaged the provisionally accepted Amejjaou track in Driouch; missing drainage and slope protections leave its durability at risk under intensifying extreme rainfall.
claims.scenario: Report warns of intensifying extreme rainfall; no named projection scenario is specified.
claims.limitations: The report does not quantify service interruptions or affected users.

access_audit.reuse_terms: No license terms identified in inspected pages.

search_audit.query: Morocco climate vulnerability named regions drought floods water scarcity oasis fisheries adaptation primary report
search_audit.outcome: Opened the full 2025 NDC, 2022-2030 adaptation plan and IFAD supervision report; found named regions, livelihood zones, project sites and group-specific exposure.

search_audit.query: Morocco climate drought water scarcity migration displacement livelihoods women rural labor primary source
search_audit.outcome: The NDC and World Bank model explicitly connect climate-related livelihood and water stress to internal displacement or possible migration; no violence pathway is inferred.

search_audit.query: Morocco conflict violence insecurity displacement disrupt climate adaptation project primary report
search_audit.outcome: No directly read primary passage linked violence or insecurity to interrupted climate adaptation. The IFAD report marks fragility/security risk non-applicable; the NDC has no conflict match.

search_audit.query: Morocco climate adaptation resilience capacity irrigation early warning local institutions IFAD report
search_audit.outcome: Read proposed regional and community adaptation measures, modeled irrigation-efficiency support, and current IFAD project delivery and infrastructure findings.

gaps: The reviewed primary sources document climate-related displacement, rural migration pathways and gendered livelihood pressures, but none establishes armed conflict, organized violence or insecurity as a climate mediator in Morocco.
The NDC's 2026-2035 mobility-reduction measures are planned benefits, not measured migration outcomes; national displacement totals are not allocated to specific events or localities.
The World Bank water and labor estimates are 2020 model scenarios based on a 2016 baseline, not observed subnational impacts or current employment conditions.
IFAD's project supervision reflects a November 2025 mission. Its reported beneficiary reach differs across sections, so the discrepancy is retained rather than reconciled by assumption.
